messages:
Matt: Canary for adaptive-prefetch v2 finished — quick summary: short-chat p99 down ~18% (420ms -> 344ms), avg token cost -9%. No user-facing errors in 10k request canary.
Anya: omg nice. where's the dashboard + PR?
Matt: dash: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/abc123/prefetch-v2  PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821
Sree: what's the memory/eviction story? any increased GC or OOMs?
Matt: memory +2% per pod on avg, hit ratio +14pp so net tail work reduced. zero OOMs in canary. evictions down ~22% at 10k sample.
Jordan: config changes? will defaults flip? any risk for Dedicated customers?
Matt: introduces flag `prefetch.policy=delayed_adaptive` (default FORCED=false). rollout plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% progressively. Dedicated customers can opt-in via config, we won't change defaults for Private without notice.
Sree: tests? perf harness?
Matt: PR has unit tests + perf bench script (`tools/bench/prefetch_v2.sh`). bench repro steps included in PR body.
Anya: add changelog entries — customers might ask about sudden cost drops. also update release notes.
Matt: will add changelog and a short customer-facing blurb.
ops-bot: canary monitor snapshot created: p50/p95/p99 + token_econ graphs look green. starting staged rollout job.
Matt: rollout playbook (short): enable 10% now -> observe p50/p95/p99 & token_econ for 30-60m -> promote to 50% if stable for 1h -> 100% after 3-4h if no regressions. Abort if p99 regresses >5% or error rate +0.1% above baseline. I'll put this in the runbook.
Jordan: I suggest we also watch worker CPU steal & NVME IO during the 50% step — prefetching could increase IO bursts.
Sree: noted; I'll add alert suppression windows and a temporary dashboard panel for IO p95.
Anya: tag eng-sre and support in release notes so oncall knows expected signal.
Matt: tagged `eng-sre`, `support`, and `customer-success` in PR. @here :rocket:
deploy-bot: staged rollout kicked off: 10% of runtime pool tagged `prefetch-v2` (job r-20260323-71).
Jordan: great. please capture a short postmortem template in case we need to rollback.
Matt: will create a tiny postmortem template in the release PR and link in the runbook. thanks team!
